A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, A Little Human Data Goes A Long Way, with complete main text and Appendices A–E. Text comparison, rendered-page inspection and matching embedded figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original fine-tuning experiments comparing human and synthetic training data for fact verification and question answering, including performance, robustness and data-property analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including the performance curves in Figures 1–4 and the detailed experimental results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The few-shot generation pipeline, label conditioning, LoRA fine-tuning and model procedures remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices B and E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight primary FV/NLI and QA datasets, Arabic/Georgian/Indonesian X-Fact splits, and cross-dataset evaluation scenarios. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same human-only, synthetic-only and mixed-data training comparisons are retained throughout the main experiments and appendices. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Training sizes, synthetic proportions, human test splits, model configurations and metrics are unchanged. This includes the 95%, 97.5% and 100% synthetic experiments with 5,000 training examples, or 500 for SciFact.

E4.justification: Appendices A and D retain the same metric, model, prompting and sample-size analyses, multilingual and out-of-domain tests, cost tradeoffs, and examinations of data properties and model errors.

E5.justification: Table 4 still reports runs 0–2. The run-wise plots and Table 1's mean, median and percentile summaries are unchanged, with no added or revised uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 3 reports CoQA BLEU of 47.9 at 0% synthetic data and 18.2 at 100% in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 4 retains the same logarithmic performance fit and inverse calculation for equivalent synthetic sample counts. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about performance declines near fully synthetic training, gains from small amounts of human data, and the relative cost-effectiveness of human annotation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of diversity, extractiveness and in-domain benefits are unchanged. The same qualifications concerning language dependence, data leakage, extrapolated cost estimates and inconclusive error analysis remain.

D1.justification: Section 10 newly discloses use of Jetstream2 at Indiana University through ACCESS allocation CIS240665. This adds computing-resource provenance; Appendix E's hardware configurations, hyperparameters and code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The added computing acknowledgment introduces no related-work citation; the bibliography merely reflows across pages.

P1.justification: V3 adds one acknowledgment paragraph and updates the arXiv version/date text. The scientific prose, terminology, section order and appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 8, 10, 20 and 21 are displayed smaller and repositioned within their pages, retaining identical panels and captions. Printed page numbers are removed, and the acknowledgment addition shifts the reference layout.

improvement.justification: The added Jetstream2/ACCESS acknowledgment improves resource attribution, while the scientific evidence, reasoning and limitations remain identical. Smaller appendix panels provide more whitespace at the expense of label size. These limited attribution and presentation edits leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
